cells.name: Continuity and responsiveness
cells.example: T4, T5 and T8 each answer the immediately preceding mind by name.
cells.limitation: T9 and T11 ignore prior turns; T12 never answers T10 or T11.

cells.name: Development of ideas
cells.example: T11 adds the current-commute baseline; T10 adds the goal-funded condition.
cells.limitation: No later turn uses T11's baseline; T12 reverts to the T1 framing.

cells.name: Exploration of central tensions
cells.example: T4-T5 weigh money buying future time against time lost now.
cells.limitation: Commute costs eroding the 25%, commute mode, remote options never raised.

cells.name: Integration of perspectives
cells.example: T10 Essentialist narrows her view toward a goal-funded condition.
cells.limitation: T6 Stoic reframe never absorbed; T12 declares division instead of combining T10 and T11.

cells.name: Progress toward understanding
cells.example: Section E turns T11 into a conditional on current commute length.
cells.limitation: T12 ends on a generic future-versus-present preference, no sharper than T1.

cells.name: Faithful engagement
cells.example: T4 accurately restates T2's distraction claim before answering it.
cells.limitation: T10 credits the Stoic with a vital-focus claim no Stoic turn made; T8 dismisses T7 as simple.

cells.name: Substance of challenges
cells.example: T5 counters T4: commute time is gone forever, future may not arrive.
cells.limitation: Targets rarely answer; T6 reframe and T5 objection go unrebutted.

cells.name: Accuracy and support
cells.example: T1 paraphrases Bentham's opening sentence on pain and pleasure accurately.
cells.limitation: T3 time-ownership line sounds like Seneca's first letter, not Meditations (suspected).

cells.name: Calibration and transparency
cells.example: T11 marks the current commute as unknown and branches on it.
cells.limitation: Hedges in most turns, yet T8 states family constraint as fact; E says will likely outweigh.

cells.name: Intellectual honesty and revision
cells.example: T10 explicitly drops the earlier money-is-distraction claim.
cells.limitation: T10 names no argument that caused the change; T5 and T6 objections never conceded or answered.

cells.name: Identification of the actual concern
cells.example: Section A frames money versus daily time; T7 offers a deciding method.
cells.limitation: Whether the user needs the raise or wants it is never asked.

cells.name: Meaningful use of personal context
cells.example: T1 and T7 convert 90 minutes each way into 180 minutes, 3 hours daily.
cells.limitation: T7 never combines the 25% and 3 hours into an effective rate.

cells.name: Fit with goals and values
cells.example: T9 asks the user which matters more, security or daily calm.
cells.limitation: T3 and T5 project the speakers' values onto the user as given.

cells.name: Attention to constraints and stakes
cells.example: T11 treats current commute length as the constraint that sizes the change.
cells.limitation: T8 invents a family-time constraint and children the user never mentioned.

cells.name: Responsiveness to information
cells.example: T11 asks current commute minutes and states what 30 versus 60 implies.
cells.limitation: Family, commute mode, remote flexibility, financial need assumed or ignored, not asked.

cells.name: Clarification of desires and motivations
cells.example: T9 offers security and calm as alternative wants with an answerable question.
cells.limitation: Reasons for wanting the raise, need versus status or growth, never distinguished.

cells.name: Examination of assumptions
cells.example: T6 questions the assumption that commute time is pure struggle.
cells.limitation: T6's challenge is never tested by others; the gross-pay assumption is never surfaced.

cells.name: Clarification of values and priorities
cells.example: T9 names the conflict between financial security and daily peace.
cells.limitation: T12 recycles the same binary without ranking or new content.

cells.name: Recognition of fears and outside expectations
cells.example: T5 names the fear of trading the present for a future never arriving.
cells.limitation: Career expectations, financial pressure, obligation to family never explored as such.

cells.name: Agency and reflective ownership
cells.example: T9 and T11 leave the user questions to answer themselves.
cells.limitation: T12 hands back only a binary, no distinction to refine.

cells.name: Definition of the decision and options
cells.example: Section E frames accept versus decline by commute length.
cells.limitation: No negotiating remote days, trial period, relocation, or counteroffer considered.

cells.name: Explanation of tradeoffs
cells.example: T4-T5 trade future capital against non-renewable commute time.
cells.limitation: Commute fares or fuel eating the 25%, and the cost of declining, never weighed.

cells.name: Identification of decisive conditions
cells.example: T11 and E: current commute 30 minutes versus an hour shifts the verdict.
cells.limitation: T7 and E leave meaningful or significantly higher undefined; no threshold computed.

cells.name: Treatment of uncertainty
cells.example: T11 singles out current commute as the consequential unknown.
cells.limitation: Other unknowns, flexibility and commute mode, never separated as major or minor.

cells.name: Proportionate next steps
cells.example: E: compute an effective hourly rate including transit time.
cells.limitation: No low-cost test such as a trial commute or asking about hybrid days.

cells.name: Accessible language
cells.example: T7 states the hourly-rate test in plain, concrete terms.
cells.limitation: T8 garbles children evening routines; occasional abstraction in T12.

cells.name: Traceable arguments and references
cells.example: T4, T5, T8 name the mind whose claim they answer.
cells.limitation: T10's appeal to the Stoic matches no Stoic turn.

cells.name: Manageable pacing and turn length
cells.example: Twelve turns, all within 25 to 65 words.
cells.limitation: T12 closes abruptly with a recap rather than a final move.

cells.name: Distinguishable positions and voices
cells.example: Positions differ: calculation, essentialism, Stoic indifference.
cells.limitation: All three share a you-might register and near-identical turn lengths.

cells.name: Economy and sustained attention
cells.example: Most turns add one point before yielding.
cells.limitation: T4, T5, T8 open by recapping the previous claim; D and E overlap.

cells.name: Meaningful stakes and tension
cells.example: T1 sets 180 minutes of daily pain against the 25% gain.
cells.limitation: Stakes stay abstract; T8's vivid stake is invented.

cells.name: Surprise and reversals
cells.example: T10 Essentialist reverses her T2 distraction claim.
cells.limitation: T10 names no argument causing the reversal; credits an unspoken Stoic claim.

cells.name: Personality and expressive voice
cells.example: T1 Bentham opens with his sovereign-masters line; T7 let us be precise.
cells.limitation: Essentialist and Stoic speak in the same hedged advisory register.

cells.name: Memorable delivery
cells.example: T5: trading your current life for a future that never arrives.
cells.limitation: No analogy or concrete image of the commute day anywhere.

cells.name: Anticipation and emotional movement
cells.example: T10 concession briefly shifts the debate's direction.
cells.limitation: Uniform rhythm throughout; T12 we remain divided ends flat.

strengths: T11 Stoic asks the current commute length and states what a 30-minute versus hour baseline implies.
T7 Utilitarian proposes an effective hourly rate including travel, a usable method for the how-to-decide question.
T10 Essentialist explicitly drops her T2 claim and narrows to a goal-funded condition.
weaknesses: T8 Essentialist invents a family-time constraint and children the user never mentioned and argues from them.
T10 reversal names no causing argument and attributes to the Stoic a claim no Stoic turn made.
All three minds hedge with you might in most turns; options never go beyond accept or decline.

symptoms.observed: Invents family time and children's routines as the user's constraint.
symptoms.evidence: this ignores your constraint of family time

symptoms.observed: Reversal cites no earlier argument; credits Stoic with an unspoken claim.
symptoms.evidence: I drop my earlier claim that money is merely a distraction

symptoms.observed: Hourly-rate test proposed but never computed; no threshold for significantly higher.
symptoms.evidence: If the new rate is not significantly higher, the math fails

symptoms.observed: Only accept or decline; no hybrid, trial, relocation or negotiation option.
symptoms.evidence: whether you value the potential for future freedom over

symptoms.observed: All minds share one hedged advisory register.
symptoms.evidence: You might find that the commute itself is indifferent

findings.description: States the user has a family-time constraint and children; the situation mentions neither.
Time as the only thing we own resembles Seneca, Letters 1, more than Marcus Aurelius's Meditations.
Essentialist paraphrases of McKeown cannot be checked without source evidence; none quoted.

rubric_fit_notes: The user gave only two numbers; reproducible check: assuming an 8-hour day and no current commute, hourly pay including travel falls (1.25/11 = 0.114 vs 1/8 = 0.125), but the 8-hour day is not the user's fact, so I credit only the debate's failure to attempt any computation. T3 attribution is suspected from memory, not established.
question_type_note: Read as a decision question: options, tradeoffs and decisive conditions about accepting the offer were scored as written.
